eclipses.name: Lunar eclipse 2025-03-14: totality at (0, 0) vs literal NASA U2/U3
eclipses.note: Different events: site totality vs whole Moon in umbra.
eclipses.detail: Ours: first/last minute the Earth disc fully covers the Sun disc (spherical Earth, R 6371 km, no atmosphere enlargement) seen from (0, 0). NASA catalogue (Espenak/Meeus): greatest eclipse TD minus delta-T 75 s; U1/U4 from the partial duration 218.3 min and U2/U3 from the total duration 65.4 min, each split symmetrically about greatest eclipse. Different events: site totality vs whole Moon in umbra.

eclipses.name: Lunar eclipse 2025-03-14: site totality at (0, 0) vs Moon-centre umbra entry/exit
eclipses.note: Our onset and offset of full Sun cover at (0, 0) against NASA's (U1+U2)/2 and (U3+U4)/2, when the Moon's centre crosses the umbra edge.
eclipses.detail: Ours: first/last minute the Earth disc fully covers the Sun disc (spherical Earth, R 6371 km, no atmosphere enlargement) seen from (0, 0). NASA catalogue (Espenak/Meeus): greatest eclipse TD minus delta-T 75 s; U1/U4 from the partial duration 218.3 min and U2/U3 from the total duration 65.4 min, each split symmetrically about greatest eclipse. A site near the Moon's centre is fully shadowed while the Moon's centre is in the umbra, from (U1+U2)/2 to (U3+U4)/2.

eclipses.name: Lunar eclipse 2025-03-14: site totality contains NASA U2 to U3
eclipses.note: Full Sun cover at the site must start no later than U2 and end no earlier than U3, because the whole Moon is in the umbra between those times.
eclipses.detail: Ours: first/last minute the Earth disc fully covers the Sun disc (spherical Earth, R 6371 km, no atmosphere enlargement) seen from (0, 0).
